newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES START WEEK LARGELY EASIER.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES START WEEK LARGELY EASIER.

text.p: Zimbabwe's short-term trading rates were quoted largely softer on the back of liquidity in Monday's quiet market, dealers said.

They said the central Reserve Bank auctioned 91-day treasury bills worth Z$400 million to a market flush with cash at an average discount of 24.86 percent, with the central bank paper was being sold on the secondary market at 24.75 percent from Friday's 24.80 percent.
NCDs maturing after 30, 60 and 90 days were being bought at 26.60 percent, slightly down from 26.75 percent and sold at 25.5 from 26 percent.
Bankers acceptance bills were stable at 25.5 percent (buying) but eased to 24.75 from 25 percent on the selling side while call money was at 22 percent from around 24 percent.
